reason: Verified in source and by driving owner-editing. render-b.js:503-513 removes the row with item.remove() and calls place(measureEl) only: nothing is pushed to history, paintUndo is never called, and closeEditor(root,false) leaves focus nowhere. Driven at file://.../master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing: items 7 -> 6, .b-undo stays data-empty="true" and display:none, Ctrl+Z afterwards leaves the count at 6, document.activeElement is BODY. So the one destructive action on the surface is the only action outside the reversibility system that already guards a one-day move, and it is offered with no confirmation, one tab stop from Done, at the same height and border. Driving also found two consequences the finding did not name, both worse than what it did name. (1) The keydown handler is bound to root (render-b.js:522), so once focus falls to body the keydown never reaches it: after a delete Ctrl+Z is dead for the rest of the session, not merely useless for the delete. Reproduced: move +7, delete, Ctrl+Z, the bar still reads data-empty="false" with the old sentence. (2) A history entry that names the deleted item survives the delete, so the bar keeps offering "Undo" for a moment that no longer exists; pressing it pops the entry, finds no node, restores nothing, and clears the bar. Reproduced: move +7, delete, click .b-undoAct, count stays 6 and the bar empties. Pressing Undo and having nothing be undone is a worse failure than having no Undo. Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs asserts only "delete removes the moment" and "the measure reflows after a delete". TASTE SEAT, on this finding’s distinct second proposal (move “Delete this moment” out of the Done row onto its own quieter line): the adjacency it names is real and measured, but the treatment it prescribes is wrong. Driven at 1440 and 390 in owner-editing: Done and Delete are peers in one .b-editActs flex row 10px apart, both 15px/400, both 35px tall, identical :hover (border --fore-46 + --fore-06 fill), and the destructive control is 157px wide against Done’s 61px — so by area the largest, and the most fitts-reachable, thing in the row is the one that destroys work; it is also the tab stop immediately after Done. Separating it is right. But (a) “beneath the sheet’s bottom rule” names an object that does not exist — .b-edit is a 12px-gap grid with only its outer 1px --fore-28 border and 16px padding; the fix silently requires drawing a divider that is not there; and (b) “the 13 step and the 0.62 alpha” is the quietest type the system permits (0.62 is stated in shell.css as the floor for letters). Deleting a moment from a draft plan is ordinary editing an owner does repeatedly, not a once-ever account nuke, so the Vercel-style danger-zone demotion is the wrong precedent; and in a palette with no red, ink density and position are the ONLY carriers of consequence — spend them on separation, not on erasure. At 13/0.62 with no border it reads as caption text beside the mono labels, loses the .b-act 32px+ hit area if built as bare text, and hides a control the owner legitimately needs to find. Separate it; do not hide it.
sharpenedFix: Store the LIVE NODE. Not outerHTML, not the record. setAway (render-b.js:317-348) writes the owner's edits to the DOM only -- data-away, data-date, the .b-away and .b-date text, the recomputed .b-grab aria-label -- and never back to F.milestones, so rebuilding the row from the record returns the moment at its fixture date and fixture visibility, i.e. it restores something the owner never had. outerHTML round-trips those attributes today but is a strictly worse copy: it re-parses, breaks node identity that the older history entries and any open editor reference, and goes silently wrong the first time anyone hangs a node-level listener or a JS property off a row -- which the editor already does for the buttons it builds. The listener worry that motivated the question does not apply here: no .b-item or .b-grab carries a per-node listener; every owner gesture is delegated on root, and the editor is appended to .b-editHost, a sibling of the rows. The node is safe to hold and is the only faithful copy. So: in the delete branch of wireOwner, before item.remove(), push {kind:"delete", id, title: record.title, node: item} onto history and call paintUndo(root). Give paintUndo a branch on kind (default the existing move sentence) reading 'Last change: ' + title + ' removed.' Give undo() a kind==="delete" branch that appends last.node back to root.querySelector('.b-measure'), calls place(measureEl), and focuses its .b-grab -- appending the same node with the same data-id also makes any older move entries for that item replayable again, which a rebuilt row would not guarantee against an open editor. Then fix the focus and the stale entry: at delete time focus the .b-grab of the nearest remaining item, or [data-act="add"] when the list is empty, so focus never reaches body; and additionally move the keydown listener from root to document (still guarded by the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable check) so a single future focus escape can never silently kill Ctrl+Z again. Do NOT add a confirmation dialog -- a reversible delete plus a named sentence is the better answer at this bar and keeps the one-gesture rhythm. Extend interaction-check.mjs with: delete is undone by the bar button, delete is undone by Ctrl+Z, the bar names the removal by title, document.activeElement is not document.body after a delete, and no history entry survives that names a row not in the DOM. TASTE SEAT sharpening of the placement half: keep it a real button — .b-act, min-height 32 (35 as measured), the 15 step, never 13. Take it out of .b-editActs and make it the last child of .b-edit on its own left-aligned row, preceded by a 1px var(--fore-16) hairline spanning the sheet’s inner width with 12px clear above and below, so the Done row closes and the destructive line begins after a visible break rather than 10px to the right of the safe action. Quiet it by removing its border and setting its rest colour to var(--fore-72) — one rung down, still plainly a control — with :hover restoring the border at var(--fore-46) and the --fore-06 fill; do NOT take it to the 0.62 floor. The separation, not the erasure, is what stops it competing with Done. Add to interaction-check.mjs: the delete control is not a sibling of [data-act="done"], its top edge clears Done’s bottom edge by at least 24px at 390 and 1440, and its measured hit box is at least 32px tall.
